newsitem.title: BELGIUM: French plan to cut VAT on CD-Roms illegal, EU says.
newsitem.headline: French plan to cut VAT on CD-Roms illegal, EU says.

text.p: France's desire to cut Value Added Tax on multimedia services is illegal under European Union VAT rules, a European Commission spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

She quoted EU taxation chief Mario Monti as telling French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis on Monday that the plan could not be allowed and that France had little chance of convincing its EU partners to change the existing tax rules.
"Monti recalled that under the current legislation it is not possible to apply a reduced rate to multimedia," the spokeswoman told the Commission's daily news briefing.

French President Jacques Chirac said earlier this month he would ask Prime Minister Alain Juppe to reduce VAT on multimedia services and products like CD-Roms to 5.6 percent. France's standard VAT rate is 20.6 percent.
EU legislation on VAT includes national lists of products or services which can benefit of a reduced VAT rate. Multimedia is not one of them.
The spokeswoman quoted Monti as telling Arthuis that "he did not see the possibility of changing the situation since this would require unanimous approval" by EU finance ministers.
But the issue may be discussed again as part of the on-going reform of the EU's VAT rules, she quoted Monti as saying.
An attempt by the French authorities in 1996 to reduce VAT on audio tapes and discs also failed due to opposition from other EU countries.
